description: Held-out split for benchmark A. NOT blinded: the same agent system that implements Git Why also authored these cases. Do not read this file from any tuning script. See bench/README.md for the honesty note.

cases.query: A user shows up twice in the "who is online" list after they reconnect from a second tab. Where was that addressed?
expectedEvidence: src/presence/roster-view.js: names collection switched from an array (push) to a Set (add) to dedupe.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Fix duplicate message dispatch after reconnect
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Same fixture, same general theme (reconnect duplication), but fixes socket-pool dispatch, not the visible roster list.

cases.query: When a call to an upstream provider times out, is there any chance the same request actually gets sent a second time in the background?
expectedEvidence: src/retry/idempotent-retry-policy.js: aborts the timed-out attempt before starting the next one.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Avoid refreshing the auth token on every retry attempt
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Same subsystem and same retry loop, but about token refetching, not about the request itself firing twice.

cases.query: There is a case-insensitive check for the Authorization header — why is that needed?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: mobile app versions <= 4.2 on Android send the header name lowercase due to a WebView quirk; keep until those versions drop below 1% of sessions.

cases.query: Why does the Acme client bother parsing the response body even when Acme returns a 200 status?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: Acme returns HTTP 200 with { error: "rate_limited" } in the body instead of 429 (confirmed via their support ticket #88213).

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Never retry Initech 501 responses
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: A different provider with its own, differently-shaped status-code quirk.

cases.query: What did the client SDK use to do for reconnect backoff before it was simplified?
expectedEvidence: Commit removed a hand-rolled exponential backoff loop that lived inline in ChatSocket.connect().

cases.query: Did workers used to ask the queue for work on a timer instead of having work pushed to them?
expectedEvidence: src/worker/poll-legacy.js (removed): pollForWork() had idle workers poll for work every 50ms before submit() pushed work directly.

cases.query: Is the CSV export code still around, or was it removed after the streaming change?
expectedEvidence: buildCsv() deleted as a follow-up once every caller used streamNdjson().

cases.query: Is there any Redis-based locking code left in the pipeline after the move to Postgres locks?
expectedEvidence: src/locking/redis-lock.js deleted once all callers moved to withAdvisoryLock().

cases.query: AuthSessionProvider cache miss metric
expectedEvidence: Emits auth_session_provider.cache_miss on a cache miss in AuthSessionProvider.getSession().

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Add dispose() to AuthSessionProvider to clear its cache
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Same class, adds dispose(), not a metric.

cases.query: AuthSessionProvider dispose cache
expectedEvidence: dispose() added to AuthSessionProvider to clear its internal cache.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Emit a metric from AuthSessionProvider on cache miss
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Same class, adds a metric, not dispose().

cases.query: Is there a minimum Node version required specifically for the streaming export code?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: Node 16's ReadableStream.from() drops the final chunk under backpressure; Node 18+ required for streamNdjson().

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Require Postgres 14+; drop support for Postgres 13
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: A version requirement in the same fixture, but about Postgres, not Node.

cases.query: Did we ever remove support for building with webpack 4?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: the webpack 4 compatibility branch in build.js had not been exercised by CI in three months; removed.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Require npm 9+ for the lockfile v3 format
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: A different tool-version requirement (npm, not webpack) in the same fixture.

cases.query: Is PresenceTracker still called that, or was it renamed?
expectedEvidence: src/presence/tracker.js (class PresenceTracker) renamed to src/presence/room-presence.js (RoomPresence).

cases.query: The Acme client file used to be named just acme-client.js — where is it now?
expectedEvidence: src/providers/acme-client.js renamed to src/providers/acme-payments-client.js.

cases.query: There is a change to the Globex client around handling a 204 with a Retry-After header -- can you find it?
expectedEvidence: src/providers/globex-client.js: callGlobex() now waits out Retry-After on a 204 before retrying (subject was just "fix 2").

cases.query: Why did the release-notes generator get bumped to a new major version?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: the new major version writes per-version changelog files instead of rewriting one CHANGELOG.md, which plays better with the release script's diff-based sanity check.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Pin esbuild to 0.19.2 pending a Windows path-handling fix
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Another lockfile-only commit in the same fixture, but about a bundler bug, not the release-notes tool.

cases.query: There was some IE11-specific caching for CORS preflight requests at some point -- when did that come and go?
expectedEvidence: Introduced: IE11's fetch polyfill re-sent an OPTIONS preflight per request; cached the preflight response client-side for IE11.
Removed: IE11 dropped from the supported browser matrix; cache deleted.

cases.query: I noticed a misspelled field name being sent in some API responses at one point -- what was that about, and is it gone now?
expectedEvidence: Introduced: app versions <= 3.0 read response.sucess (typo) instead of response.success; mirrored the field under both keys.
Removed: app version 3.0 and earlier can no longer authenticate at all after a certificate pin rotation; mirrored field deleted.

cases.query: Why does the Acme provider client check the response body for an error field even on a successful-looking status?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: Acme returns 200 with { error: "rate_limited" } in the body instead of 429 (support ticket #88213).

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Bump the Globex token expiry buffer from 30s to 90s
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: A different provider (Globex) whose issue is clock skew on token expiry, not response body shape.

cases.query: Why doesn't the gateway ever retry against Initech when it gets a 501?
expectedEvidence: Commit message: Initech uses 501 to mean "billing account not yet provisioned" (their docs section 9), which resolves over minutes/hours, not something a short retry backoff would ever catch.

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Bump the Globex token expiry buffer from 30s to 90s
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: A different provider and a token-timing issue, not a status-code retry rule.

cases.query: Why does WorkerPool track a "busy" counter instead of a set of individual worker objects?
Why is the AuthSessionProvider cache TTL exactly 30 seconds rather than, say, 60?

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: AuthSessionProvider: cache getSession() results for 30s
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Introduces the 30s TTL but never justifies the specific number.

cases.query: Why is the retry policy's max attempt count a fixed constant instead of configurable per provider?
Why is the minimum supported Node version 16 rather than 18 for this project?

whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.subject: Require npm 9+ for the lockfile v3 format
whyDistractorsAreNotAnswers.reason: Bumps the npm floor and explains why, but never touches or justifies the Node floor.
